title: What Do Blood Pressure Numbers Really Mean?
description: Systolic (top) and diastolic (bottom) numbers explain heart strain—120/80 is ideal for adults 35+, but 130/85 raises stroke risk by 30%. Learn what’s safe—and when to act.
reasoning: People are suddenly searching this because rising hypertension rates, at-home BP monitor adoption, and new AHA guidelines (emphasizing lower thresholds for adults 35+) have created widespread confusion—especially around 'normal' ranges, isolated elevations, and age-specific risks. Users want plain-language clarity, not medical jargon, to interpret their own readings and decide if action is needed.
perplexityQuestions: What do bp numbers mean, and which number is systolic vs diastolic?
Is 140/90 dangerous at 45, or is it just slightly high?
What does it mean if my top number is 130 but bottom number is normal?
What does it mean if my bottom number is 90 but top number is under 120?
Is 120/80 really normal for adults over 35?
